id.description: Pin this job to a build ID, from `build.id` on a job response or `GET /v1/simc/builds`. The build must be from the last 30 days and on the requested branch; if it is unavailable when the job runs, the job falls back to `channel`.

text.description: SimC profile text, as you would run it locally. Maximum 5 MB (UTF-8).

multiStage.description: Run the sim in stages, culling profilesets between them. Defaults to a single pass.

maxCredits.description: Spend cap for this job, in credits. A job that reaches it is stopped with `errorCode` `max_credits_reached` and billed the cap. The maximum is `plan.maxCreditsPerJob` on `GET /v1/simc/usage`.

maxRuntimeSeconds.description: Deprecated: use `maxCredits` (`maxRuntimeSeconds × 32`). Do not send both.

maxQueueSeconds.description: Seconds this job may wait in the queue before it is cancelled. Defaults to `plan.defaultQueueSeconds`, up to `plan.maxQueueSeconds`, on `GET /v1/simc/usage`. `economy` jobs get a longer default and maximum. The response returns the value applied as `runtime.ceiling.queueSeconds`.

runtime.description: Execution options. Multistage is skipped if your input has directives it does not support.

priority.description: Higher priority runs first; equal priorities run in submission order. Defaults to `plan.defaultPriority` and is capped at `plan.maxPriority`, both on `GET /v1/simc/usage`. `high` adds a per-job fee only when it buys a faster start, reported in `runtime.priorityFeeCredits`.

workload.description: `interactive` (default): starts as soon as capacity allows, for sims someone is waiting on. `batch`: bulk work that may queue for hours; set `runtime.maxQueueSeconds` to cover the wait. `economy`: runs at reduced speed and uses none of your daily full-speed time. Only the workloads in `plan.workloads` on `GET /v1/simc/usage` are accepted.

metadata.description: Your own labels, returned unchanged (for example `profileSource`, `characterRef`).

json.description: JSON report options. A JSON report is always generated.

artifacts.description: Output formats to produce. Logs, the input and a JSON report are always produced. For multistage runs, HTML covers only the final stage.
